title.narrative: Protection assistance to Sudanese refugees in Libya

description.narrative: With the continuous arrival of Sudanese refugees in Libya, urgent life-saving assistance is needed to ensure protection risks are minimized for Sudanese refugees registered with UNHCR. Registration with UNHCR is the basis for obtaining an asylum-seeker certificate, allowing identification and specific needs assessments for further referrals and targeted assistance. As of July 2024, UNHCR is only allowed to register in Tripoli, thus the geographic focus of the project is on life-saving assistance to Sudanese refugees in Tripoli. Advocacy is conducted to extend registration to other parts of the country, especially locations where Sudanese are arriving, however, there are no indications by authorities that this might be approved in the coming months.Through CERF support, the period between taking an appointment and actual registration is planned to be minimized to about one month period. After registration of newly arrived refugees, the focus of the activities in this project is on protection needs assessments (PNAs) and for unaccompanied or separated children on best interest assessments (BIAs). This will allow referrals to specialized services and case management, not only for UASC but also refugees with other vulnerabilities, such as gender-based violence (GBV) survivors or psycho-social support. With fast-track registration of particular urgent cases, such as medical cases who need life-saving or urgent health services (highly pregnant women, etc.), UNHCR registration allows immediate assistance, however, UNHCR also ensures that refugees independent of their nationality are treated equally.Compared to the overall registered Sudanese refugee population, an increase of female headed households arriving more recently is observed, requiring additional and targeted protection assistance. This includes GBV assistance through case management and targeted assistance through a survivor-centered approach but also engagement with communities to identify and subsequently assist survivors who would not be willing to reach out for help. A concerning increase of GBV survivors is noticed, especially since people fleeing from neighboring Darfur are reaching Libya, thus requiring urgent assistance. While in Libya, the refugee population live in urban contexts, cash assistance to at-risk refugees is of life-saving importance to be able to address basic needs, however, is severely impacted by the on-going liquidity and banking challenges. UNHCR operates emergency cash assistance through vouchers which will allow refugees to purchase needed items at pre-identified vendors.
